title: Operator intake checklist + automated network-and-upgrade autoscorer for private/VPC/on-prem
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a standardized operator-facing intake checklist and an automated autoscorer that evaluates incoming private/VPC/on-prem deployment requests for network-readiness, upgrade compatibility, and air-gapped constraints. The autoscorer will power deterministic routing into remediation lanes (Self-Serve, Assisted Onboarding, Eng Remediation, Blocked) and provide an estimated engineering effort and recommended next steps.

Goals: (1) reduce manual triage time for PM/RSE by 60% on first-touch requests, (2) provide consistent, reproducible intake outcomes, (3) surface high-risk requests early with suggested mitigations, (4) enable a soft-launch of the tool with three pilot customers.

Scope: intake form schema + operator checklist, scoring engine (rule-based initially), webhook integration with support portal, auto-generated preflight report (PDF/Confluence link), and basic dashboard metrics (score distribution, time-to-route). This ticket covers the PM requirements, acceptance criteria, and pilot rollout plan; engineering tickets will be created for implementation.
comments: 2026-02-10 - Asha Patel: Created ticket. Initial hypothesis: many onprem requests fail the same 6 checks (egress allowlist, upgrade window, KMS access, proxy/mtls, kernel modules, shrinkwrapped firmware). Proposal: encode these checks as discrete weighted rubrics and emit a numeric score (0-100).

2026-02-12 - Luis Moreno: Reviewed. Recommend starting with a rule-based engine (deterministic) before moving to ML. Suggested score buckets: 0-39 Blocked, 40-59 Eng Remediation, 60-79 Assisted, 80-100 Self-Serve. Add a 'confidence' bit when customers provide proof artifacts (eg. firewall dump, upgrade approval).

2026-02-14 - Design review (Maya Chen): Operator UI mockups look good; prefer compact card view with quick actions (request probe, request logs, schedule call). Added accessibility note for long error messages.

2026-02-16 - Security (Ravi Singh): Security review required for any automated probes that touch customer networks. Proposed constraint: probes must be opt-in and use customer-provided egress endpoints; add consent checkbox to intake form. Also require PR for probe agent 3rd party audit.

2026-02-17 - PM prioritization meeting: Decided soft-launch with three customers (enterprise A: regulated finance, enterprise B: healthcare, enterprise C: adtech) to validate false-positive rates. If >20% false positives we will tighten rules. Also decided to publish the rubric to customers as 'preflight checklist' to reduce friction.

2026-02-18 - Engineering triage (Kiran Patel): Split into implementation epics: intake API + UI, scoring engine service, probe orchestration & agent, reporting/PDF generator. Engineering estimates: intake/UI 2 pts, scoring engine 3 pts, probe infra 5 pts (separate ENG tickets will be created).

2026-02-19 - Asha Patel: Added acceptance criteria and pilot measurement plan to Confluence. Success metrics: median triage time <= 2 business hours for routed requests, pilot NPS from customers >= 7, and >50% of incoming requests qualify for Self-Serve or Assisted without eng intervention.

2026-02-20 - Luis Moreno: Decision log - we will not attempt automated remediation in phase 1. Only generate remediation tasks and recommended playbooks. Phase 2 will explore automation (eg. ephemeral proxy bridge).
